claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to understand your situation. 

**First, let me ask about the child or children you want to claim Child Benefit for:**

How old is the child (or what are the ages of the children) that you're claiming for?

The key age thresholds are:
- **Under 16 years old** - generally qualifying
- **16-19 years old** - may qualify if they're in certain education or training
- **20 years or older** - typically not eligible

Please tell me the age(s) of your child/children, and I'll guide you through the rest of the eligibility checks.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Yes, I'm interested in claiming Child Benefit and would like to know if I'm eligible.

I have one child - Alex is 3 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 3 years old, which means he qualifies as a qualifying child for Child Benefit purposes.

Now let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Since Alex is 3 years old, he wouldn't be working. Let me move forward with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is Alex receiving any of these benefits in his own right:**
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit

Or to put it simply - is Alex receiving any state benefits directly in his own name?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in his own name. He's only 3, so nothing like that applies to him.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's clear. Let me continue with the next check:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Since Alex is only 3 years old, he's not in any apprenticeship. Let me move forward:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency situation. **Do any of the following apply to you:**

1. **You normally live in the UK** - This is the most common route
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme AND:**
   - You're working and earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months, OR
   - You're actively seeking work (up to 91 days), OR
   - You have sufficient resources to support your family without claiming certain benefits, OR
   - You're a student with sufficient resources, OR
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad** in certain qualifying countries

Which of these describes your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I normally live in the UK. I live here with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That confirms you meet the residency requirements. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to confirm your responsibility for Alex. **Which of these applies to you:**

1. **You live with Alex** - You have him living with you
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** - You pay for things like food, clothes, housing, or pocket money for him (at least the equivalent of the Child Benefit amount)
3. **You pay maintenance** - You pay maintenance for Alex under a court order or agreement

What's your situation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's clear - you live with Alex. Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is anyone else going to claim Child Benefit for him?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent (if applicable)
- A grandparent or other relative
- Anyone else who has responsibility for Alex

Or are you the sole person who will be claiming for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Where is Alex living? Please tell me if any of these apply:**

1. **In hospital** - Alex is in hospital as an inpatient
2. **In care** - Alex is in local authority care or accommodation
3. **Fostered** - Alex is being looked after by a foster parent
4. **Living normally at home** - Alex is living with you at home as normal

Which applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is living normally at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**One final check: Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words:
- Is the local council providing or paying for Alex's housing/accommodation?
- Is the council contributing financially to Alex's care or upkeep?

Or are you covering all of Alex's costs yourself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything. I'm covering all of Alex's costs myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That means you've passed all the eligibility checks. Let me now provide you with the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Now let me confirm your eligibility:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## ✅ **You ARE ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!**

Congratulations! Based on all the information you've provided, you meet all the eligibility requirements to claim Child Benefit for **Alex**.

### **Summary of Your Eligibility:**
- ✅ Alex is 3 years old (a qualifying age)
- ✅ Alex is not working full-time
- ✅ Alex is not receiving any benefits in their own right
- ✅ You normally live in the UK
- ✅ You live with Alex and are responsible for him
- ✅ No one else is claiming for Alex
- ✅ Alex is living normally at home
- ✅ The local council is not paying towards Alex's care

### **Next Steps:**

To claim Child Benefit, you need to:

1. **Apply online** at [www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim) or **by post using form CH2**

2. **Prepare the following documents:**
   - Proof of your identity
   - Proof of Alex's identity
   - Alex's birth certificate or adoption certificate

3. **Important note:** If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may be subject to the **High Income Child Benefit Charge**, which may reduce or eliminate your benefit

4. **Payment arrangements:** Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

For more information, visit: [www.gov.uk/child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit)

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
